blocks.text: XII. The twelfth passage is Es. XXII, 17, where the Prophet says to Shebna, יהוה מטלטלך טלטלה גבר, The Lord will carry you away with a carrying away, O man. Others render with the carrying away of a man, that is, they say, a manly, strong, vehement one. But this version has two drawbacks. The first is that no example of this expression is adduced. For when we read elsewhere of the way of a man, the sorrow of a man, the redemption of a man, the teaching of a man, no one understands vehemence. We only infer from it that these things either are in a man or proceed from a man. Thus the carrying away of a man would be nothing but that by which a man carries away or is carried away, which would be very weak. Besides, the carrying away of a man would be expressed in Hebrew as טלטלת גבר, not טלטלה. For who would grant what some assert here, that the final He in טלטלה is epenthetic and not the mark of the feminine, since this too is without example? Finally, the accent tiphcha on טלטלה suspends the voice and prevents it from being joined with the following גבר. Clearly, then, גבר is in the vocative case, as if it read אתה הגבר, O you man. This Aben Ezra and Kimchi rightly observed. And long before them the Syriac translator, who has: ܡܪܝܐ ܡܛܠܛܠ ܠܟ ܛܘܠܛܠܐ ܓܒܪܐ, The Lord will surely cast you out, O man. Yet there are some among the Hebrews who render, The Lord will carry you away with the carrying away [II, 687] of a man, or even with the carrying away of a cock. For although the word גבר, very frequent in Scripture, everywhere else means man, here they chose to do violence to the sacred text and interpret it as cock, compelled by no necessity but only by an itch and bad habit of καινοτομία [kainotomia]. Hence on the words טלטלה גבר R. Selomo has כהדין תרנגולא דמטלטל מאתר לאתר, Like a cock that is carried from place to place. This is taken from the Midrash on the Psalms, as Kimchi observes. Accordingly Jerome here has: The Lord will make you be carried off, as a cock is carried off. This, of course, follows the view of that Jew from whom he had learned Hebrew letters, as he himself notes in his Notes, where he paraphrases (παραφράζει [paraphrazei]) this passage thus: And I say this, that you should not labour at hewing out a sepulchre, because the Lord will transfer your priesthood, as גבר is wont to be transferred, which all have interpreted as man. But the Hebrew who instructed us in the reading of the Old Testament translated it cock. “As (he says) a cock is transferred from one place to another on the shoulder of a carrier, so the Lord will lightly carry you away from your place”. Accordingly in the Talmud גבר is sometimes used for cock, as when they say קריאת הגבר for cockcrow. And in the tractate On the Sabbath, p. 67b, גברית is the same as תרנגלת, hen. Indeed, among the paraphrasts Jonathan calls Ezion-geber כרך תרנגולא, the fortress of the cock, Num. XXXIII, 35. 36. and Deut. II, 8., as if Ezion-geber were named from a cock, whereas עציון גבר is the spine of a man. That Ezion-geber was called by this name we have shown in our Phaleg, p. 764, because it is situated in a place inaccessible because of reefs and rocks (ῥαχίαις καὶ σπίλοις ἀπροσίτῳ [rhachiais kai spilois aprositō]), like Dyrrachium in Macedonia. And what is read of Balaam in Num. XXIV, 3., נאם הגבר, The man said, Baal Hatturim takes as if it read The cock said, and taking occasion [col. 119] from this he draws a ridiculous comparison of Balaam with a cock in these words: קרא גבר שדומה בלעם לתרנגול כמו שהתרנגול הוא נואף מכל כן בלעם רבע אתונו וכמו שהתרנגול יודע בעתים כן בלעם יודע לכוין השעה שהקב״ה כועס וכמו שהתרנגול דרכו לעמוד על רגל אחד כן בלעם חגר באחד רגליו, He calls him גבר, because Balaam was like a cock. As the cock is lecherous above all, so Balaam lay with his she-ass; as the cock knows the times, so Balaam knew how to find out the hour at which God, the Holy One, blessed be He, is angry; as the cock is wont to stand on one foot, so Balaam was lame in one foot. Most absurd of all is this: although the other sacrifices which God had prescribed in his Law have now been abolished, yet on the day preceding the feast of Atonement there is no one among the Jews who does not offer a cock for himself, repeating these words while he strikes it against his head three times: זה חליפתי זה תחתי זה כפרתי זה התרנגול ילך למיתה ואני אלך לחיים טובים עם ירשאל אמן, Let this cock be an exchange for me; let this be in my place; let this be an atonement for me; let this cock go to death, but I, with all Israel, to a happy life. Amen. For the rest, consult the distinguished Buxtorf's Synagoga, chapter 20. Here it suffices to add that the occasion of the error was the ambiguous word גבר, by which they hold that both man and cock are signified. It is fitting, therefore, they say, that since גבר has sinned, גבר [II, 688] should bear the penalty of the sin. As if a cock and a man could be held as one before God's tribunal because, through an abuse of the word, they are called by the same name. I deliberately pass over what is found about the cock in the second Targum of Esther, because these are not paraphrases but the author's mere fabrications.
